_comment: L1 plan Task 14 (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-14-l1-curated-library.md): Burgmüller, 25 Etudes faciles et progressives Op. 100, Nos. 4 and 6 to 18, engraved by Bas Wassink for the Mutopia Project from the Collection Litolff edition (public domain). Facts from content/tools/candidates.json and the fetched RDF; retrievedAt is the fetch log's date. Fields as documented in catalog.json's _comment. Tempo marks: the engravings print only the tempo word; the metronome values are compared with the 'Original Tempo' of the PTNA Piano Encyclopedia (enc.piano.or.jp, commentary by Takashi Sato, retrieved 2026-10-14). Levels: Henle's per-piece levels for Op. 100 (HN 1726, https://www.henle.de/en/25-Etudes-op.-100/HN-1726, retrieved 2026-10-14; Henle 1 is about our 2, Henle 2 about our 3), Burgmüller's progressive order, the core pieces Nos. 1, 2, 3, 5 at our levels 2, 3, 3, 3, and level.py's proposal. Rule: the plan's level is kept unless Henle's placement and the heuristic both disagree with it (Nos. 9, 12 and 17 move from 4 to 3).

pieces.title: La Styrienne (Styrian Dance)
pieces.tempoSource: LilyPond \midi block of the source (quarter = 176); the engraving prints Tempo di Valse; the same as the original mark quarter = 176 (PTNA Piano Encyclopedia, https://enc.piano.or.jp/en/musics/23989)

pieces.notes: Engraved from the Collection Litolff edition, including its fingerings. Litolff subtitle: Steierischer Tanz, Styrian Dance. The two catalog patches change only LilyPond's MIDI, not the score: the piece opens with a grace note in each staff (a slashed C# and a spacer), which shifts LilyPond's whole MIDI timeline by 43/384 of a quarter, so the MIDI is rendered from a second \score block without those two grace events (tagged layout). The MusicXML is byte-identical with and without the patches; the published Mutopia MIDI keeps the same constant shift (0 of 310 onsets match, an accepted difference).

pieces.title: Ballade
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: the original mark for the printed Allegro con brio, dotted quarter = 104 in 3/8, that is quarter = 156 (PTNA Piano Encyclopedia, https://enc.piano.or.jp/en/musics/23990); the source's \midi block has quarter = 104, the dotted-quarter value entered as a quarter, a third slower than the mark
pieces.levelNote: Level 4: Henle level 2 (HN 1726) is about our 3, but the heuristic proposes 4 (score 9.46: repeated three-note chords at dotted quarter = 104, 17 percent accidentals), so the plan's 4 is kept
pieces.notes: Engraved from the Collection Litolff edition, including its fingerings. One catalog patch removes the \bar "||" that the source writes just before \repeat volta 2 at bar 31, because it hid the start-repeat bar from which the converter derives the repeat, so the MusicXML now has the forward repeat (unfolded order: bars 1 to 46, 31 to 46, 47 to 96) and the notes are unchanged.
